blogs.title: Standing with FOIA: The D.C. Circuit’s Tightening of the Procedural Injury Standard
blogs.description: The court’s analysis of America First Legal Foundation’s Article III standing is a treatise on how courts apply the procedural‑rights doctrine to FOIA disputes. Read how the decision flips the “injury in fact” test, requires concrete informational harm tied to the statutory right, and limits speculative causal chains. This post also discusses why the Court chose not to evaluate redressability, and what the ruling means for NGOs and public‐interest plaintiffs who hope to rely on procedural‑right claims for standing in FOIA litigation.

blogs.title: OSC’s Enforceability Puzzle: Mandatory vs. Discretionary Power Under § 1216(a)(3)
blogs.description: AFL’s argument that OSC owes a mandatory investigation under § 1216 runs right into the statutory labyrinth of 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(F)(i). This article dissects the Court’s interpretation that OSC’s authority is discretionary unless the precise triggers of FOIA’s enforcement clause are met. We explore how Congress intended OSC to function, how the court reconciles the Civil Service Reform Act with FOIA, and why the decision leaves OSC out of the “must‑investigate” category.

blogs.title: Using OSC as a Trump Card? Practical Lessons for FOIA Litigants in the Wake of the Ruling
blogs.description: With the court clarifying OSC’s limited investigational role, what does that spell for plaintiffs who want to compel the Office of Special Counsel to act against alleged FOIA missteps? This post evaluates the strategic implications for public‑interest groups, the feasibility of filing FOIA suits that lean on OSC enforcement, and the alternative avenues—direct FOIA claims, bad‑faith requests, or the Merit Systems Protection Board—that might yield more predictable redress.

blogs.title: The Interagency Chain: OSC, MSPB, and DOJ – How an Office’s Decision Fuels or Blocks Redress
blogs.description: The ruling’s discussion of causation and redressability opens a window onto the administrative mechanics of a FOIA enforcement cycle: OSC investigation, potential MSPB corrective action, DOJ’s decision to release records. We unpack the Court’s emphasis on the speculativeness of agency decisions, the limits of judicial compulsion of independent actors, and how litigants must align their expectations with the realities of inter‑agency enforcement. This analysis is essential for anyone looking to navigate the complicated overlap between OSC, MSPB, and DOJ.
